Admission.description: Whether new messages are admitted. It closes once, in the seal (or at finalize or cancel), and never opens again.

ApiError.description: Error body for every non-2xx response.

ApprovalDecision.description: Answer to a relayed permission request (`--approvals relay`).

Authority.description: Who wrote an event: the deterministic harness or an (untrusted) agent.

ClaimRefusal.description: Why the server would not hand out a message.

oneOf.description: A run-level Cancel is queued: it wins, and the pending messages end `rejected` with `run-cancelled`.
The seal closed admission: nothing is pending and nothing will be.

ClaimRequest.description:
`POST /internal/message-claim`: "give me the next pending message of this session". With `messageId` it claims that message (a `now`
message agentd was told about); without it, the oldest `now` message, else the oldest `next` message, in server order. `limit` (1 to
[`MAX_CLAIM_BATCH`], default 1) takes several at once. A claim is one conditional write per message, fenced by `generation` and `epoch`.

ClaimResponse.description:
The answer to a claim. The fencing errors (a stale generation or session) are HTTP 409 with their own codes, not an outcome: they mean
this agentd must stop acting on messages.

oneOf.description:
The messages are `dispatching` now and belong to this generation, interrupts first, then oldest first.

`redelivered` is true when these are messages this generation claimed earlier and has posted no outcome for: the retry of a claim whose
answer was lost. agentd that already sent one of them must not send it again; it posts the outcome it has.
Nothing is eligible in this session.
The message named is not pending any more (withdrawn, claimed, rejected ...): `state` says what it is.

ClaimedMessage.description: A message agentd claimed: its text, which agentd sends exactly once.

attempt.description:
Which claim of the message this is: 1 for the first, one more each time a claim was given back (`released`) and taken again. The
outcome names it, so a late retry of an earlier attempt's outcome cannot settle a later attempt. A redelivery repeats the number.

CompletenessEntry.description: One declared range of loss or exclusion.

CompletenessKind.description:
Why a range of the stored conversation is not shown in full. The words a writer may declare; the reader adds two of its own
(`unreadable`, `missing`) that are never written.

oneOf.description: Thoughts, binary output and replayed history: left out on purpose.
A size cap cut it.
The writer shed it under load.
Redaction withheld it.
Storage failed.
Another writer held the key, or two writers overlapped.
An older image stores no transcript.
A writer ended without a final flush.

nonce.description: The rotating nonce from the previous response.

Envelope.description: One event in the run log (DynamoDB `EVT#<runId>#<shard>`, sort key `eventId`).

EventType.description: Event types in architecture table order.

EventsBatchRequest.description: A batch of agent events. Stored with `authority=agent` only.

takeControls.description:
`false` on a turn's final flush: the response carries no controls, so they stay queued for
the next turn. Absent means the response carries them.

FaultHint.description:
Structured evidence of a provider fault, as agentd reads it from the ACP error data (Cline
patch 0011, OpenCode) or from its own watchdog. Every member is optional; a hint with none set
is the same as no hint.

code.description: A short machine code: `stall` from the watchdog, else what the engine named.

silentS.description: For a stall: how long, in seconds, the engine was silent.

FaultTransport.description:
Where in agentd the engine failure was seen: only failures on the engine transport can be
infrastructure-unknown; agentd-local ones (worktree, engine start, credential socket,
write-policy) set none and keep the ordinary failed-turn path.

oneOf.description: The engine answered a request with a JSON-RPC internal error (-32603).
Reading or writing the engine's pipes failed.
The engine closed its output.

FetchFailure.description: One URL of a fetch that produced no item.

FetchRequest.description:
`POST /internal/research/fetch`: each URL must already appear in this run's search results, in the prompt or as a link of a page the
run fetched (the provenance gate).

query.description: What the caller wants from the pages; Tavily returns focused chunks (smaller files).

InstructAction.description:
What the user (or, later, the analyzer) asks the machine to do. Wire words: `continue_with_prompt`, `new_session_with_prompt`,
`try_model`, `finish`. One control carries all four so a person and the analyzer share one path.

InstructOrigin.description: Who answered. control-api always writes `user`; `analyzer` is written only inside agentd.

ItemRef.description:
A stored item as an answer names it: where its manifest and body are, and the hashes the reader checks. Content is never in an
answer.

licence.description: The SPDX id of the licence, or `NOASSERTION`.

manifestSha256.description: SHA-256 of the manifest's canonical bytes ([`ItemManifest::sha256`]): the item's index hash.

JobRequest.description: `POST /internal/research/job`: ask after a job. Another run's or agent's job answers `not_found`.

JobResponse.description: The answer to `repo` and to `job`: HTTP 202 while the job is queued or running, 200 once it has ended.

pollAfterMs.description: While pending: when to ask again.

JobState.description: The state of an asynchronous job (a repository download).

LimitsRequest.description:
`POST /internal/research/limits`: read-only; it touches no counter and calls no upstream. A run with research off gets the
`disabled` error, which is how agentd learns not to start its loopback server.

enabled.description: Always true in an answer: a run with research off gets the `disabled` error instead.

expiresAt.description: Epoch seconds after which the policy row refuses every call.

oneOf.description: At the end of the current turn, as its own user turn (the default).
Now: agentd cancels the current turn, waits for it to settle and prompts on the same session.

MessageNotice.description:
A pending message as agentd is told about it: no text (the claim returns that). It is handed out in every events response while the
message is pending in the current session; the hand-out changes nothing, so it can repeat, and agentd treats a repeat as the same message.

epoch.description: The session it is pending in.

MessageOutcome.description: What agentd tells the server about a message it claimed (or, for `rejected`, one it will not take).

oneOf.description: The prompt was sent to the engine in `turn`: `dispatching` becomes `delivered`.
The message was not sent and cannot be: `dispatching` becomes `failed`. `detail` is cut to [`MAX_DETAIL_CHARS`].
The claim is given back (an interrupt that could not cancel the turn): `dispatching` becomes `pending` again, in mode `next`.
agentd will not take it: `pending` or `dispatching` becomes `rejected`. Only the reasons [`RejectReason::agent_may_set`] names.

MessageState.description:
The status of a message, as the server holds it. HTTP 202 on the send means `pending` and nothing more: Cline has not
read the message yet. `delivered` means agentd sent the prompt to the engine, not that the engine acted on it.

oneOf.description: Durably accepted and eligible: it will be claimed at the end of the turn (`next`) or now (`now`).
Pending when the session changed: it waits for the user to confirm it again and never makes the run wait.
agentd won the claim and is submitting it.
agentd reported sending the prompt; `deliveredTurn` names the turn.
The user withdrew it before it was claimed.
The run could not take it; `reason` says why.
A confirmed copy replaced it (the only way into this state).
agentd could not submit it (it was never sent); `detail` says why.
It was claimed, then the worker was lost before the outcome was known: it may have reached Cline. It is never sent again by itself.

attempt.description: The `attempt` of the claim this answers ([`ClaimedMessage::attempt`]); for `rejected` of a message agentd never claimed, 0.

epoch.description:
The session agentd is in now. It is informative: an outcome is fenced by the incarnation and the attempt, because a session may
change between a claim and its outcome.

OutputPin.description: What agentd knows about one object it wrote.

sha256.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the bytes agentd sent. S3 stores the same digest as the object's checksum, so a reader can compare it
without downloading the body.

versionId.description:
The version id S3 returned for agentd's own write. Absent when the answer carried none (an unversioned bucket); the digest then
has to hold on the current version.

OutputPins.description:
The records of the objects one turn wrote. Each member is present when agentd's write of that object was answered; an object that was
not written has none.

Payload.description: Event body: inline JSON up to [`MAX_INLINE_PAYLOAD_BYTES`], or a claim check on an S3 object.

PendingControl.description: Controls waiting for the agent, delivered in the events response.

oneOf.description:
Protocol 1.37.0: a person's (later the analyzer's) answer to a `needs-input` question of a
direct run. The `ControlItem`'s `control_id` is the request id, which is the nonce: one answer per request.

model.description: `try_model` only: a route id of this run (the `models` list of the question).

text.description: `continue_with_prompt` needs it; `new_session_with_prompt` and `try_model` take it optionally; `finish` takes none.

oneOf.description:
Protocol 1.38.0: a message of the user is pending in the current session. worker-api adds one to the `pending` list of
every events response while the message is pending; it is a notice (no text), it is never stored as a control item and handing it out
changes nothing, so it repeats until agentd claims the message (`POST /internal/message-claim`). An agentd built before 1.38.0 sets the
item aside (`lenient_pending`) and acts on the rest of the list.

Refusal.description:
One kind of permission request agentd's role policy refused in a turn: the tool, what the
first such request asked for, agentd's reason, and how many requests of the turn got it.

action.description:
The first such request's command or paths, the worktree path shown as `.`, control
characters escaped, secrets redacted; at most [`MAX_REFUSAL_ACTION_CHARS`] characters.

count.description: Requests of the turn refused with this tool and reason (1 or more).

reason.description: agentd's reason, the same way; at most [`MAX_REFUSAL_REASON_CHARS`] characters.

tool.description: The tool the engine named (`run_commands`, `editor`, `read_files`), `-` when none.

RejectReason.description: Why a message was rejected. Every reason but `engine-busy` and `continuation-limit` is the server's alone.

oneOf.description: The run was sealed: it ended or was ending when the message was about to be sent.
The user stopped the run; a Cancel wins over a message.
agentd could not take the message into its queue.
The run's Agent registered no message control (a run on an older image).
The allowance of message-driven turns after "done" is used up.
A limit (the cap on messages or bytes of one run).

RepoRequest.description:
`POST /internal/research/repo`: download one GitHub repository at a ref as a job. The idempotency key is required: the route starts
the job once per key.

paths.description: Keep only these path prefixes (at most [`MAX_REPO_PATHS`]); absent keeps the whole filtered tree.

ref.description: A branch, a tag or a commit; absent means the default branch. The manifest records the commit id the archive carries.

ResearchError.description:
The body of a non-2xx answer: the shape of [`crate::api::ApiError`] plus a retry hint, so a client that reads only `code` and
`message` works. Also the `error` of a failed job and the reason of a failed URL in a fetch.

message.description: One plain sentence; never a key, a header or fetched text beyond a short excerpt.

ResearchErrorCode.description:
The closed set of words a research route answers with when it does not do what was asked. Each has one HTTP status (the route's
answer), and one `ham-research` exit code (2 usage, 3 policy, 4 limit, 5 upstream). The words are the product's: a client shows
them and a test pins them.

ResearchLimits.description:
The per-run limits. They are abuse and exfiltration bounds, not budgets (spend is approved), settable in the stage configuration and
copied into the run's policy row when the run starts. `Default` is the numbers

callsPerMinute.description: Calls of any kind per minute and run.

contextBytes.description: Bytes of all research material of one run.

outboundBytes.description: Bytes of model-chosen outbound text (queries, URLs, repository paths) per run.

repoCompressedBytes.description: Bytes of the filtered archive that is stored.

repoDownloadBytes.description: Bytes downloaded for one repository archive.

repoReadBytes.description: Bytes read from one archive after decompression, kept or not.

repoUnpackedBytes.description: Bytes of the files kept from one archive.

ResearchProvider.description:
Where an answer came from. The stage configuration chooses the search provider; a caller cannot. Every response, audit object and
manifest records it, so each record can be checked against the provider the stage is configured for (`tavily`
unless the stage names another).

ResearchUsage.description: What a run has used so far. The route's counters are conditional updates, so concurrent calls cannot pass a cap.

RuleDelivery.description: How a rule reaches the engine.

oneOf.description: The engine loads the file itself.
Written into agentd's compiled rules file.

source.description: A repository-relative path, a rule name, or `system prompt`.

oneOf.description: Harness invariants, carried by the supplied system prompt.
Tenant and run rules sent with the run.

`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.clinerules/**`, `.cline/rules/**`, `.roo/rules-<role>/**`,
`.cursorrules` in the repository.
The role's customInstructions.

RulesManifest.description: The per-session rules manifest: every rule in precedence order and how it was delivered.

compiledSha256.description: SHA-256 of the compiled rules file, when one was written.

oneOf.description: "Anything pending? if not, the run is done": pending messages come back; none closes admission.

The allowance of message-driven turns is used up: pending and held messages end `rejected` with `continuation-limit`
and admission closes.

The run is ending whatever is pending (shutdown, finalize): pending and held messages end `rejected` with `run-sealed`, a
dispatching one becomes `delivery-unknown`, admission closes, nothing comes back.

SealRequest.description:
`POST /internal/message-seal`: agentd's last question before it declares the run done, and its closing call at shutdown. The server
answers with one conditional write.

oneOf.description: Eligible messages exist in this session, in server order: agentd claims and sends them, then asks again. Admission stays open.
Admission is closed. After this a send is 409 `run-sealed` and stores nothing. `watermark` is how many messages the run admitted.

deliveryUnknown.description: Dispatching messages this seal turned into `delivery-unknown`.

rejected.description: Pending and held messages this seal rejected.

SearchDepth.description: Tavily's search depth: basic costs 1 credit, advanced 2.

idempotencyKey.description: A repeat with the same key and the same body returns the first answer; the same key with another body is `conflict`.

id.description: `s-0001`: the search record under `searches/` holds what was shown.

SearchResult.description: One search hit. `snippet` is cut to 1 KiB by the route and is third-party text: a client marks it untrusted.

deliveryUnknown.description: Messages this report moved from `dispatching` to `delivery-unknown`.

epochNo.description: The number of the session within the run.

held.description: Messages this report moved from `pending` to `held`.

SessionReport.description:
`POST /internal/message-session`: agentd tells the server which incarnation of agentd (`generation`, a ULID made at its start) holds
which session (`epoch`, the engine's session id). An incarnation the server has not seen replaces the current one, unless its ULID is
older than the current one's by more than [`GENERATION_CLOCK_SKEW_MS`]; one the server has replaced is refused for good. The server
commits it before any later claim: a message pending in an older session becomes `held`, a message the replaced incarnation was
dispatching becomes `delivery-unknown`.

number.description:
The ordinal of this session within the incarnation: 1 for its first session, then 2, 3 ... A report whose number is lower than the
last one of the incarnation is the late retry of an older report and changes nothing; the same number with another `epoch` is refused.

TimeRange.description: A search restricted to recent pages.

TranscriptSummary.description:
What the worker declares at `turn-complete` (protocol 1.38.0): the last chunk it stored and what it left out or lost. It is the
worker's report, written by a process the engine can reach; the state `complete` means "the worker reports no loss".

TurnCompleteRequest.description: End of a turn. It carries no verdict: the harness gates and evaluates independently.

faultHint.description:
What agentd could tell about a provider fault that ended the turn:
structured evidence for the goal step's classifier. Absent for every turn that ended
without one and for an agentd that sets none.

finishReason.description: Engine finish reason, recorded as telemetry only.

handoff.description:
`true` when the slice ended at its prompt deadline and the invocation said more time was left (`slice.last` false): the work is
committed, bundled and uploaded, and the service starts the next slice. Absent for every other end, so an agentd that predates the member
is read as a slice that ended the run.

maxSilentGapS.description:
The longest silence, in seconds, between two engine updates in the turn (1.22.0): the data
for tightening the stall budget.

outcome.description: How the turn ended as `agentd` observed it: telemetry, never a verdict.

outputPins.description:
What agentd knows about the three end-of-run objects it wrote: the SHA-256 of each body and the version id S3
gave to its own write. Only a call that carries the run's completion key reaches `SendTaskSuccess`, so the engine cannot set this; worker-api
drops the member from a call that did not prove the key. `plan-delivery` and the bundle validator read exactly these versions. Absent
from an agentd that predates the member.

refused.description:
The kinds of permission request agentd's role policy refused this turn, grouped by tool and
reason with secrets redacted; the goal step lists them in the agent's
next prompt. At most [`MAX_REFUSALS`] ([`cap_refused`]); absent when none.

refusedTruncated.description: `refused` left kinds out or shortened a field.

reverted.description:
Repository paths the engine changed outside the role's write globs, which agentd restored
before the commit;
build outputs of the role's own commands are not listed. At most [`MAX_REVERTED_PATHS`],
each at most [`MAX_REVERTED_PATH_CHARS`] characters ([`cap_reverted`]); absent when none.

revertedTruncated.description: `reverted` left paths out or shortened one.

rulesDigest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `rulesManifest`, when an engine ran.

rulesManifest.description: The turn's rules manifest: every rule in precedence order and how it was delivered.

summary.description:
The agent's final message of the turn (its text, control characters removed, the last
[`MAX_TURN_SUMMARY_CHARS`] characters): a read-only task's report, a claim otherwise.

transcript.description:
What the transcript writer declares: the last chunk it stored and what it left out or lost.
Absent from an agentd that writes no transcript.

usage.description: Engine-reported tokens; absent when the engine reported none.

TurnOutcome.description: How a turn ended, as `agentd` observed it. Telemetry only: the harness owns "done" (invariant 1).

sigv4.description: AWS Signature Version 4 (API Gateway AWS_IAM authorization).
sigv4.name: Authorization

info.title: Hyperscale Agent Meta Harness internal API

post.summary: Re-mint session credentials after the goal, session and nonce checks
Store agent events; returns pending steer, cancel and approval answers and the notices of pending messages
SendTaskHeartbeat for the caller's open turn
agentd claims pending messages before it sends them: one conditional write each, fenced by generation and session
agentd reports that a claimed message was submitted, failed, released or rejected
agentd asks whether anything is pending; if not, admission closes in the same write
agentd reports its incarnation and its session (the epoch); messages pending in an older session become held
Fetch pages the run has seen as stored research items; served by research-api
Ask after a research job; served by research-api
Read the run's research limits and use; research-api answers disabled when research is off for the run
Start the download of one public GitHub repository as a stored research item (a job); served by research-api
Search the web through the stage's research route (Tavily); served by the research-api Lambda, not worker-api
SendTaskSuccess for the caller's open turn; carries no verdict
